name: נגזרת של e^((x−xⁿ)^(1/k)) (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Find the following derivative:

\( \displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[{{CT:1}}] = \) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Use the chain rule twice: once for the exponential and once for the power inside it.
Step 1 — The chain rule for the exponential
To solve this question, you will have to use the chain rule more than once.
The chain rule: \( \frac{d}{dx}f(g(x))=f'(g(x))\,g'(x) \)
Let \(f({{CT:0}})={{CT:1}}\) and \(g({{CT:0}})={{CT:2}}\). Then, \(f({{CT:0}})=e^{(g({{CT:0}}))}\)

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[{{CT:1}}] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{df}{dg}\cdot \frac{dg}{dx} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{dg}(e^{g})\cdot \frac{d}{dx}[{{CT:2}}] \end{array} \]

Step 2 — The chain rule for the power
To find

\[ \frac{d}{dx}[{{CT:2}}] \]

you have to define a new function: \(h({{CT:0}})={{CT:3}}\), so that \(g({{CT:0}})=h^{{CT:4}}\). So,

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[{{CT:2}}] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{dg}{dh}\cdot \frac{dh}{d{{CT:0}}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{dh}(h^{{CT:4}})\cdot \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}({{CT:3}}) \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:4}}h^{{CT:5}}\cdot ({{CT:6}}) \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:7}} \end{array} \]

Step 3 — Putting it together
So,

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[{{CT:1}}] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{dg}(e^{g})\cdot \frac{d}{dx}[{{CT:2}}] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle e^g \cdot {{CT:7}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle e^{{CT:2}}{{CT:7}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:8}} \end{array} \]
